activity_context.topic_title: Defining Definite Integrals Using Left and Right Riemann Sums

feedback.problem: What is ${\int }_{3}^{4}5{x}^{2}\text{d}x$ expressed as the limit of a right Riemann sum?
feedback.worked_solution:
The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a right Riemann sum as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx,
$$

where ${x}_{i}=a+iΔx$ and $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}.$

In the definite integral

$$
{\int }_{3}^{4}5{x}^{2}\text{d}x,
$$

the function is $f(x)=5{x}^{2},$ the lower bound is $a=3$ and the upper bound is $b=4.$ So, we have

$$
Δx=\frac{4-3}{n}=\frac{1}{n}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{3}^{4}5{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}[f(3+i\cdot \frac{1}{n})\cdot \frac{1}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}[f(3+\frac{i}{n})\cdot \frac{1}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}[5{(3+\frac{i}{n})}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{n}].\end{aligned}
$$
